chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about buying from the land of the Jews and Christians, so he said: 'There is no harm in it. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) conquered the people of Khaybar and made a treaty with them to leave the land in their hands, so they would work it and cultivate it, and there is no harm in it. And if you buy something from it, and whoever people revive a piece of the land or work it, they are more entitled to it, and it is for them.'

key_terms.فَخَارَجَهُمْ: and made a treaty/concord with them

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy land from Jews and Christians in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the purchase of land from Ahl al-Kitab by invoking the precedent of the Khaybar treaty, where the Prophet Muhammad allowed Jews to retain ownership and cultivation rights in exchange for tribute. It establishes the principle of *ihya al-ard* (reviving the land), asserting that those who work and develop the land hold superior rights to it, a concept foundational to Shia jurisprudence regarding property rights and economic interactions with non-Muslims.
